body: Mumbai investor from a Kolkata broking family (Kedia Securities); began as a trader and has spoken publicly about early-career losses in the 1990s before shifting to long-term holding. Framework: SMILE - Small in size, Medium in experience, Large in aspiration, Extra-large market potential. Widely cited past winners (media lists; entry prices and multiples not verified here): Atul Auto (three-wheelers, held for over a decade), Aegis Logistics, Cera Sanitaryware, Vaibhav Global, Elecon Engineering, Tejas Networks, Sudarshan Chemical, Precision Camshafts. Folklore: claims that a small early stake in Atul Auto or Aegis turned 1 lakh into crores circulate widely but have no documented entry dates/prices - treat as unverified. Edge: process - concentrated holdings in small companies with ambitious, hungry promoters and a large addressable market, held for years; he meets managements and stresses promoter integrity and 'hunger'. Mistakes: like all small-cap concentrators, several holdings have halved in drawdowns; some later bets (turnaround infra/engineering names) took years to work. Copyable: the SMILE checklist is a reasonable small-cap screen when paired with balance-sheet and governance filters; size each idea so one failure does not matter.
title: Vijay Kedia - SMILE small-cap growth investing (India)
